title: Small Sample Rink
pitch: The NHL's 84-game season opened on 2026-09-29, so fans are reading early records like 3-0-1. A visitor sets a fictional team's start and games played, and a worker grows an orchard of thousands of simulated seasons, each one a fruit hanging at its final point total, so the spread shows what a hot or cold start can and cannot tell you. A regression receipt itemises how many points of the start are likely luck, and a Call the Season game scores the visitor's gut against the simulation. Everything is simulated, with invented teams and labelled assumptions.
whyNow: The 84-game NHL season opened on 2026-09-29, so early records are being read closely right now. The sampling mechanic works for any season length and any start, so it stays useful all winter.

research.summary: As of 2026-10-10, several independent outlets (NHL schedule release, AP wire copies, ESPN, Pollstar, DailyFaceoff, theScore) report that the 2026-27 NHL regular season began Tuesday 2026-09-29 with 84 games per team, 1,344 games in total, ending Saturday 2027-04-10; AP describes it as the first 84-game-per-team schedule since 1993-94, so it is not a league record per team. Independent explainers agree on the points rule (2 for a win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss, 0 for a regulation loss, in place since 1999-2000), which creates the extra variance the simulator models. One analytics write-up (single outlet, unconfirmed) reports that top-10 first-month teams made the playoffs far more often than bottom-10 teams over 2014-15 to 2023-24. The model is deliberately fictional: invented teams, adjustable talent and overtime assumptions, all labelled as simulation rather than league data.

facts.claim: The 2026-27 NHL regular season began on Tuesday 2026-09-29.
Each of 32 teams plays 84 games in 2026-27 (1,344 games in total, 42 home and 42 road per team), the first 84-game-per-team schedule since 1993-94 per AP, so it is not a record per team.
The 2026-27 regular season ends on Saturday 2027-04-10.
NHL standings award 2 points for a win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss and 0 for a regulation loss.
The overtime-loss point entered the NHL points scheme in 1999-2000.

design.coreLoop: The visitor enters a record (wins, overtime losses, regulation losses) and games played, and adjusts a belief slider for how much of the start is real talent. A worker simulates thousands of remaining seasons; fruit on a branch show the final-points spread, a playoff-line slider shows the share above the line, and the regression receipt itemises luck versus skill. Scrubbing games played from 4 to 40 shows how slowly the spread narrows, which is the surprise that rewards the tenth minute. A Call the Season mode scores the visitor's guesses against fresh synthetic starts with a streak and calibration score.
sophisticationHooks: Monte Carlo in a web worker with a four-outcome game model (regulation win, overtime win, overtime loss, regulation loss) and a talent prior that shrinks toward the league middle as the sample grows
Orchard visual: each simulated season as a fruit at its final points, with density rings and a playoff-line cut
Regression receipt and a hash-encoded share link of a team's start
Call the Season prediction game with calibration scoring and a streak
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: seeded simulation worker (with a main-thread fallback), canvas orchard, controls with keyboard and touch, receipt view, Call the Season game with streak, season-length selector (82 and 84), hash state, about panel, light and dark, reduced motion. Cut: real team rosters or records, live standings, real schedules, strength-of-schedule modelling, the real-team preset, the first-month playoff study unless shown as reported and unconfirmed. Suggested order: worker and model first, orchard second, receipt third, game last; the game is the first thing to cut if time runs short.
risks: No live or real team records are bundled; all teams are invented, and any mention of the real season start and length is shown as 'as of 2026-10-10, per AP and the NHL schedule release'.
The season is described as 84 games per team, the first such schedule since 1993-94 per AP; the page must not call 84 games a league record per team.
The overtime share, talent spread and default playoff line are model assumptions, not NHL data; the page labels them as such and says 'simulated, not advice' next to any odds.
The first-month playoff study (79 of 100 versus 28 of 100) rests on one outlet; the page shows it as 'as of 2026-10-10, per The Hockey Writers, reported and unconfirmed' or omits it.
Real team names, logos and art are not used; fictional teams keep the page clear of brand issues. Playoff odds are for fun and carry no wagering or betting framing.
Another hockey simulator may be proposed by other scouts, so the orchard-and-receipt framing is the distinguishing angle.
Verification used search results only; the ESPN host could not be fetched, so no source was opened.

verification.notes: Season dates, the 84-game length and the points rule are confirmed by several independent search results; the dossier's claim that 84 games is a league record was wrong (first since 1993-94) and the first-month playoff study stays single-outlet. Scope is achievable by 8 agents in a morning if the game is the cut line and the simulation is seeded and fully local.
